methodological_rigor.justification: The design is a retrospective, multi-cohort bioinformatic signature-building study (TCGA training N=234; GSE30219 N=78; GSE31210 N=168; FUSCC N=70) with downstream in vitro validation of DEGS1/PLOD1 in two LUAD cell lines, which is appropriate for prognostic-index development but inherently susceptible to overfitting and selection bias. Strengths include external validation across three independent cohorts, use of multiple ML algorithm combinations with C-index-based selection, multivariable Cox adjustment, and in vitro functional confirmation. Important weaknesses: the authors explicitly concede that nested cross-validation / hyperparameter tuning was not performed, risking optimistic performance estimates; the median-based cutoff is derived from the training cohort and applied without recalibration or an a priori threshold; no sample-size or power calculation is reported, and the scRNA-seq validation rests on only nine patients; multiplicity correction across the many pathway, immune, drug, and mutation comparisons is not described beyond generic adjusted P values; handling of missing clinical covariates in multivariable Cox is not addressed; preclinical replicates are limited (n=3-5) and blinding of migration/proliferation scoring is not stated.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Design maps to an individual retrospective prognostic cohort study with external validation and supportive preclinical mechanistic work, consistent with Oxford LoE 2b. The clinical question — refining risk stratification beyond TNM in stage I LUAD to guide adjuvant decisions — is genuinely important and the endpoints (DFS, OS) are patient-relevant. However, all therapeutic implications (paclitaxel, bortezomib, vincristine; immunotherapy benefit) are in silico predictions from GDSC/CTRP/CMap/TIDE/IPS/SubMap without prospective or even retrospective clinical treatment-outcome correlation, and the authors themselves label these hypothesis-generating. Translational path is plausible but not demonstrated, warranting a mid-range score.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is the most applicable standard given the biomarker/prognostic focus (TRIPOD is a reasonable alternative for the prediction-model aspect). Most REMARK items are addressed: patient sources, inclusion/exclusion (>3 month follow-up), assay source (public expression data), model-building procedure, validation cohorts, multivariable adjustment, and subgroup analyses are reported. Gaps include absent reporting on handling of missing data, lack of a formal flow diagram, no pre-specification/registration, no calibration assessment beyond discrimination (C-index/AUC), and limited reporting of adverse events (NA here) or clinical-utility metrics. Data availability is moderate: all discovery/validation cohorts are public with GSE/EGA/TCGA accessions and R packages are cited with versions, but no repository/code location for the MAPI implementation itself and no primary data for the knockdown experiments are stated in the retained text.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is incremental: metabolism-focused prognostic signatures for LUAD and specifically for early-stage LUAD have been published (the authors themselves cite Hu et al. Front Oncol 2021 and Zhu et al. Front Immunol 2022), and the Mime1 'ten-algorithm combination' workflow has been widely applied to TCGA to produce near-identical signatures across cancer types. Marginal advances are the stage-I-restricted scope, triangulation across WGCNA + ML + scRNA-seq + in vitro knockdown, and functional nomination of DEGS1/PLOD1. However, PLOD1 and DEGS1 oncogenic roles are already documented in multiple cancers (HCC, gastric, thyroid, head-and-neck, as the discussion acknowledges), and no first-in-class mechanism, new assay, or paradigm-shifting observation is introduced.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear Introduction–Methods–Results–Discussion flow, an informative structured abstract, and figure legends that are generally self-contained and quantitatively specific (e.g., AUC values enumerated per cohort and time point). Acronyms are expanded on first use (WGCNA, MAPI, TIDE, IPS, CMap, OCLR, mRNAsi) and the Discussion appropriately contextualizes limitations including the absence of nested CV and the hypothesis-generating nature of drug predictions. Minor issues: occasional typographic artifacts ('FIG 1..'), awkward phrasings ('immunologically activate'), and the Results occasionally drift into interpretive claims that would sit better in the Discussion, but overall clarity is good.

key_strengths: External validation of MAPI across three independent stage I LUAD cohorts (GSE30219, GSE31210, FUSCC/EGA) with consistent DFS/OS stratification
Multi-layered biologic characterization including metabolic pathway, stemness (mRNAsi), TMB, immune infiltration, cancer-immunity cycle, TIDE/IPS, and SubMap analyses
scRNA-seq validation linking MAPI to CytoTRACE-defined differentiation state across AIS→MIA→IAC
In vitro knockdown of DEGS1 and PLOD1 in A549 and H358 showing suppression of proliferation and migration
Transparent acknowledgment of key limitations (retrospective design, lack of nested CV, in silico drug nomination)
key_concerns: Highly incremental novelty — stage-I LUAD metabolic signatures already exist and the Mime1 ten-algorithm workflow is widely reused on TCGA
No nested cross-validation, no power calculation, and median training-cohort cutoff applied to validation cohorts risks optimistic performance
Therapeutic claims (paclitaxel, bortezomib, vincristine; immunotherapy benefit) rest entirely on in silico databases without clinical treatment-outcome validation
Multiplicity correction across the extensive pathway, immune, mutation, and drug comparisons is not clearly specified
scRNA-seq validation uses only nine patients and in vitro experiments lack reported blinding and are limited to two cell lines
No explicit code-availability statement for the MAPI implementation nor deposition of primary knockdown data
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competent, well-validated but incremental TCGA-derived prognostic signature with modest mechanistic follow-up — appropriate for a mid-tier oncology journal (Cancers / Frontiers in Oncology / BMC Cancer range) with minor revisions clarifying statistical rigor and data/code availability; novelty and reliance on in silico therapeutic predictions preclude higher-tier placement.
